title: Geometric representations of permutations
key_idea: Permutations of $[n]$ correspond bijectively to regions of the **braid arrangement** (the hyperplane arrangement $\{x_i = x_j : i<j\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$). This geometric viewpoint connects the combinatorial statistics (inversions, descents) to the geometry of the arrangement — chambers, walls, and the Coxeter group $S_n$.
summary: **To be filled in when you reach this section.** Topics: the braid arrangement $\mathcal{A}_n$, permutohedron, the bijection between permutations and regions, how descents correspond to walls, weak order on $S_n$. Motivates the broader theory of hyperplane arrangements in §3.11.

notation.description: Braid arrangement: the set of hyperplanes $\{x_i = x_j\}$ for $1 \leq i < j \leq n$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$
Permutohedron: convex hull of all $n!$ permutations of $(1,2,\ldots,n)$
